module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 258

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/258](https://www.erdosproblems.com/258)
- [Ch26] P. Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro, [Erdős problem 258](https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos258.pdf) (2026)
- [St26] ster-oc, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 258](https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean) (2026)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos258

/--
Let $a_n \to \infty$ be a sequence of non-zero natural numbers. Is
$\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{(a_1 ... a_n)}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

This was proved affirmatively by Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro [Ch26], and formalised in Lean
by ster-oc [St26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean"]
theorem erdos_258 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) →
    Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i)) := by
  sorry


/--
Let $2 \leq a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \cdots$ be a monotone sequence with $a_n \to \infty$.
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{a_1 \cdots a_n}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

Solution: True (proved by Erdős and Straus [ErSt71], Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.13).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_258.variants.monotone : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) → Monotone a →
    Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i)) := by
  sorry


/--
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where $t ≥ 2$ is an integer.

Solution: True (proved by Erdős, see Erdős Problems website)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-lean-erdos249-257/blob/a9104f2f12aa0d4e9da8a93574b14990ed02dc2a/adapters/FormalConjecturesAdapter.lean#L109-L117"]
theorem erdos_258.variants.constant : answer(True) ↔ ∀ t ≥ (2 : ℕ),
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / t^(n + 1))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos258

findings.description: The docstring says the result was "proved by Erdős and Straus [ErSt71], Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.13". The paper has no Theorem 2.13: (2.13) is a displayed inequality inside the proof of Lemma 2.2. The monotone irrationality result is Theorem 2.23, which the paper gets by combining Lemma 2.2 (slow growth) with Lemma 2.14 (fast growth). The key [ErSt71] is also missing from the module docstring's reference list. The Lean statement itself is fine; only the citation is wrong.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Straus, 'Some number theoretic results', Pacific J. Math. 36 (1971) 635–646; I read the OCR layer of https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1971-21.pdf. §2 says: "LEMMA 2.2. The series (2.1) is irrational if there exists a δ > 0 so that the inequality a_n < (log n)^{1-δ} holds for infinitely many values of n." The proof of Lemma 2.2 ends with "Combining (2.7) and (2.13) we see that ∑ is irrational." Next comes "LEMMA 2.14. If there exists a positive constant c so that |a_n| > c(log n)^… for all n then the series (2.1) is irrational." Then: "Summing up we have THEOREM 2.23. The series (2.1) is irrational whenever 2 ≤ a_1 ≤ a_2 ≤ ⋯ ≤ a_n ≤ ⋯", followed by "Conjecture 2.24. The series (2.1) is irrational whenever a_n → ∞." Chojecki's note (https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos258.pdf) also cites "[5, Theorem 2.23]" and "[5, Conjecture 2.24]".
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to "Solution: True (proved by Erdős and Straus [ErSt71, Theorem 2.23], combining Lemmas 2.2 and 2.14)." Add "[ErSt71] P. Erdős and E. G. Straus, Some number theoretic results, Pacific J. Math. 36 (1971), 635–646" to the module references.

status_issues.recorded: research solved, answer(True), formal_proof using lean4 at the ster-oc gist (689a848…/Erdos258.lean). The docstring says it was "formalised in Lean by ster-oc [St26]" and does not mention any condition.
status_issues.source_status: Solved in the affirmative (Chojecki & GPT-5.4 Pro, using Tao–Teräväinen Theorem 1.1). erdosproblems.com and the teorth database record "proved (Lean)" since 2026-04-21. However, the linked Lean file is conditional: it introduces `axiom tao_teravainen` (TT Theorem 1.1, stated there without proof). The category and answer are correct; only the `formal_proof` record is in question.
status_issues.evidence: The gist header says "modulo the deep Tao–Teräväinen theorem from analytic number theory (stated here without proof)" and declares `axiom tao_teravainen : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ (∃ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ k, 0 < k → … Ω(N+k) ≤ C * k)`. Locally, `#print axioms erdos_258` on the gist lists `tao_teravainen` (plus `sorryAx`, which comes only from version drift: the gist targets Mathlib v4.28 and this repo uses Lean v4.33.1). On the forum (21 Apr 2026), ster wrote: "I made the gist conditional on the theorem itself, namely [248], so that once the latter is formalized, the gist will become unconditional." Tao wrote (14 Apr 2026) that under the erdosproblems standard it "does not yet qualify as a formalization … but … would become so after that paper is published". arXiv 2512.01739 shows no journal reference. PROOFS.md says to check `formal_proof` links for custom axioms. Files 306, 659 and 694 describe conditional formalizations in prose without a `formal_proof` attribute, and 1148 records only an unconditional proof.
status_issues.suggested_change: Either say in the docstring that the linked formalization is conditional on Tao–Teräväinen Theorem 1.1 (declared as an axiom), or drop the `formal_proof` attribute until that theorem is formalized. Keep `research solved` and `answer(True)`.

reformulations.difference: The Lean requires `∀ n, 2 ≤ a n`, including the unused `a 0`. The source (erdosproblems.com) and the theorem's own docstring say "positive" / "non-zero natural numbers", which allows finitely many a_n = 1. (Erdős–Straus and [Er88c] themselves use a_i ≥ 2, i.e. "1 < a_1".)
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Source ⇒ Lean: immediate, since 2 ≤ a n gives positivity and `a 0` never occurs (the product runs over `Icc 1 (n+1)`). Lean ⇒ source: take a positive sequence a with a_n → ∞. Pick N with a_n ≥ 2 for all n ≥ N, and let b n = max (a n) 2. Then b ≥ 2, b → ∞, and b = a from N on. For n ≥ N the partial products satisfy P_b(n+1) = (C_b/C_a)·P_a(n+1), where C_a = ∏_{i≤N} a_i and C_b = ∏_{i≤N} b_i. So S(a) = F_a + (C_b/C_a)(S(b) − F_b), where F_a and F_b are finite sums of rationals. Hence S(b) irrational implies S(a) irrational. Both series are summable, because the terms of S(b) are at most (n+1)/2^(n+1). I proved this in Lean as `Review258b.equiv_main`: (∀ a, (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) → Tendsto a atTop atTop → Irrational S(a)) ↔ (∀ a, (∀ n, 0 < a (n+1)) → Tendsto a atTop atTop → Irrational S(a)), using the file's exact summand. `#print axioms` lists only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

reformulations.difference: The Lean requires `2 ≤ a n` for every n and `Monotone a` on all of ℕ, which includes the unused `a 0 ≤ a 1`. erdosproblems.com speaks of a positive sequence with a_{n-1} ≤ a_n (so a_1 = 1 is allowed). The Lean also keeps the hypothesis a_n → ∞, which Erdős–Straus Theorem 2.23 does not need. That makes the variant a weaker, still true, special case of Theorem 2.23. It is exactly the monotone case of the problem as erdosproblems.com describes it.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Same finite-modification argument as for the main theorem. Set b 0 = 2 and b n = max (a n) 2 for n ≥ 1. This preserves monotonicity and divergence, gives b ≥ 2, and b agrees with a from some N on. The series then differ by a nonzero rational scaling and rational shifts. Proved in Lean as `Review258b.equiv_monotone`: (∀ a, (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) → Monotone a → Tendsto a atTop atTop → Irrational S(a)) ↔ (∀ a, (∀ n, 0 < a (n+1)) → Monotone (fun n => a (n+1)) → Tendsto a atTop atTop → Irrational S(a)). Axioms: only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

could_not_verify: Erdos258.erdos_258 (formal_proof): I could not build the ster-oc gist on its intended toolchain (Mathlib v4.28). On the repo's Lean v4.33.1 several proof steps break from version drift. I confirmed by reading the source and by `#print axioms` that its `erdos_258` assumes only `∀ n, 0 < a (n+1)`, which would imply the file's statement, and that it depends on `axiom tao_teravainen`.

Erdos258.erdos_258.variants.constant (formal_proof): the wcook04 adapter theorem at L109–117 states exactly the file's proposition, and a scan of the corpus at that commit finds no `sorry` and no `axiom` declarations. I did not build the 33 MB corpus, so I did not run `#print axioms` on it.
review.notes: No misformalization found. All three statements elaborate as intended. The summands are real divisions `↑(n+1).divisors.card / ↑(∏ i ∈ Icc 1 (n+1), a i)` and `↑card / ↑t ^ (n+1)`. The series are always summable under the hypotheses, so the `tsum` junk value 0 never comes into play. Each `answer(True)` matches the affirmative answer in the source. [Er88c, p.103] (OCR) reads: \"Straus and I proved that if 1 < a_1 ≤ a_2 ≤ ⋯ is a sequence of integers then ∑ d(n)/(a_1a_2⋯a_n) is irrational; we conjectured that it suffices to assume that a_n → ∞\". So `2 ≤ a n` follows the original convention, and I proved it equivalent to erdosproblems.com's \"positive integers\". Minor attribution point: the gist's header calls it the \"original formalization by Przemek Chojecki\" (made with Aristotle), which ster-oc adapted, so the docstring's \"formalised in Lean by ster-oc\" is slightly off. The Lean proofs of both equivalences are in /workspace/review/equiv2.lean.
